definitions.explanation: Having a relaxed, generous disposition that does not get bothered by small matters. Describes someone who is tolerant and unflustered, with the composure associated with nobility or maturity.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{鷹揚|おうよう}な{人|ひと}だ。
{鷹揚|おうよう}に{構|かま}えて、{細|こま}かいことは{気|き}にしない。
examples.english: He takes things in stride and doesn't worry about the small stuff.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{鷹揚|おうよう}な{性格|せいかく}で、{孫|まご}たちの{失敗|しっぱい}にも{笑|わら}って{許|ゆる}してくれた。
examples.english: My grandfather had a magnanimous personality and would laugh off his grandchildren's mistakes.

notes: The kanji {鷹|たか} (hawk) and {揚|よう} (to raise) evoke the image of a hawk soaring high above, unconcerned with trivial matters below — a metaphor for noble composure. Common collocations: {鷹揚|おうよう}に{構|かま}える (to remain composed/unflustered), {鷹揚|おうよう}な{態度|たいど} (a magnanimous attitude). Generally a positive quality, though it can sometimes imply being too laid-back or careless. Homophone: {応用|おうよう} (application, applied use) — completely different word. Related: {寛大|かんだい} (generous, lenient — focuses on forgiveness), おおらか (easygoing — more colloquial).
